quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson defends Arizona's performance against top-tier basketball competition
quotes.excerpt: When you go to a prestigious basketball academy like Arizona, we did what we were supposed to do.
quotes.quote: When you go to a prestigious basketball academy like Arizona, we did what we were supposed to do. You held home court against another top-10, top-12 team in the country. That's expected. I'm not calling the guys being like, 'Big win guys, man, big win.' I'm like, you did what you were supposed to do. You held home court against another top-10, top-12 team in the country. That's expected. I'm not calling the guys being like, 'Big win guys, man, big win.' I'm like, you did what you were supposed to do.
quotes.social_post: Richard Jefferson on Arizona basketball: You held home court against a top 10 team. That is expected. You did what you were supposed to do.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye discusses the difficulty of guarding Amen Thompson
quotes.excerpt: He hit me with one of those his very first training camp. He's hard to guard.
quotes.quote: He hit me with one of those his very first training camp coming out of OTE. It was like the first day of training camp he hit me with one of those crossovers, so I definitely seen it up close and personal. Just hard to guard, moving very fast, and explosive and quick. Trying to sit in front of that and guard that is not a great place to be.
quotes.social_post: Channing Frye on guarding Amen Thompson: He hit me with a crossover the first day of training camp. He is just hard to guard, moving very fast, and explosive.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson reflects on his own playing style and athleticism
quotes.excerpt: I don't move my feet fast enough. I'm like a heavy-footed guy.
quotes.quote: I don't move my feet fast enough. I'm like a heavy-footed guy. I'm so glad that there's no footage of me like getting crossed up and falling, touching earth. There's no footage. Why? Because I was a feet-set person and then I would use the body. I would go to the body. That's it. I'm not trying to dance with you.
quotes.social_post: Richard Jefferson on his playing style: I do not move my feet fast enough. I am a heavy footed guy. I was a feet set person and then I would use the body. I am not trying to dance with you.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye praises Alperen Sengun's development as a power forward
quotes.excerpt: He is a prototypical in my world of like a true power forward.
quotes.quote: Alperen Sengun has been awesome this year, right? And does he know that I call him the Big Senguini? I hope he does. Anyway, he is a prototypical in my world of like a true power forward. I feel like we're getting a lot more of those guys, but he doesn't really have just one position, but he's physical, he plays, he plays both face in the basket, back to the basket, taking advantage of mismatches. He's been running the floor this year, really getting out.
quotes.social_post: Channing Frye on Alperen Sengun: He has been awesome this year. He is a prototypical true power forward. He is physical, plays both face in the basket and back to the basket, and takes advantage of mismatches.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye explains Fred VanVleet's impact on team success
quotes.excerpt: Fred doesn't need to do a lot for y'all to win. He needs to do enough.
quotes.quote: From our point of view and to the casual fan, you got to look at how Fred plays. Fred doesn't need to do a lot for y'all to win. He needs to do enough to make sure that people are happy and as he's scaling and staying healthy. Because Houston can be dangerous if everyone understands their role and accepts it and knows that they're leaders, whether that's defensive leader, offensive leader, whatever, emotional, is going to do the right play all the time. It's just after playing with Steve Nash and LeBron James and those kind of guys, Brandon Roy, they just make the right play when it's necessary.
quotes.social_post: Channing Frye on Fred VanVleet: Fred does not need to do a lot for Houston to win. He needs to do enough to make sure people are happy and stay healthy. He makes the right play when it is necessary.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye argues that team chemistry is more important than constant meetings
quotes.excerpt: Sometimes it's not as complicated as like having everybody needs to be getting along.
quotes.quote: Sometimes it's not as complicated as like having everybody needs to be getting along and everybody has to just all these kumbaya meetings and all this. Like some teams just work. Some teams just that has the right mix and the right match and we got our scores and we got K and we got Sengun and those are our main guys and everybody else going to play off of them.
quotes.social_post: Channing Frye on team chemistry: Sometimes it is not as complicated as having kumbaya meetings. Some teams just work. They have the right mix and the right match.

quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson shares his experience playing Halo 2
quotes.excerpt: Yeah, Halo 2 for me. That's how old I am.
quotes.quote: Yeah, Halo 2 for me. That's how old I am. Halo, Halo 2, let me tell you this. Halo is the greatest first-person shooter game of all time.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson details his intense dedication to Halo 2
quotes.excerpt: I played it for 8 to 12 hours multiple times.
quotes.quote: Scuba Steve. You guys might know him as Steve Senior. He is the assistant GM for the Minnesota Timberwolves. Him and I go back like four flats on a Cadillac. We were playing in Philly the night that it came out. He picked me up from Philly so I didn't have so after the game, I got in a car in Philly and drove. He wasn't even in the he wasn't even associated with the league or the Nets, but he drove to Philly to pick me up. So as soon as the game ended, I showered, I was still probably sweating, talked to the media on my way out, I got in the car, we drove straight back to my apartment and we played it for 8 to 12 straight hours. Like that's how quickly I was trying to oh, multiple times. I played it for 8 to 12 hours multiple times. I didn't have Wi-Fi setup at my house because I just bought my New York apartment. So Wi-Fi wasn't finished setting up into my house. So I went over to my friend's house. He left to go to work, so I showed up in the morning, he left to go to work. After work, he like went to the gym, did some other things, and came back and I was still in the exact same spot. Had Domino's pizza, Mountain Dew. I'm that's how locked in I was.
quotes.social_post: Richard Jefferson on his Halo 2 obsession: I played it for 8 to 12 hours straight multiple times. I would shower after a game, get in a car, and drive straight home to play.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye recalls playing World of Warcraft with teammates

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson discusses his time with the Utah Jazz
quotes.excerpt: I played a quick 82. So just so everybody knows, I played all 82 games.
quotes.quote: I played a quick 82. So just so everybody knows, I played all 82 games and I started 78 of them. We were trash, but we were trash, but mind you, this was year 13. I was coming off multiple injuries, so my whole thing is I wanted to play all 82 and I played I started in 78 of them, played all 82, caught a couple of bodies, like, and that is what got me to Dallas, which ended up getting me to Cleveland.
quotes.social_post: Richard Jefferson on his time with the Jazz: I played all 82 games in year 13. We were trash, but I caught a couple of bodies, and that is what got me to Dallas.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye discusses the evolution of NBA team defense
quotes.excerpt: The teams that are going to be there at the end are the teams that defend.
quotes.quote: The teams that are going to be there at the end are the teams that defend. We all know that. So if the teams want to do all the cute stuff, but how about this, Perk? Can we switch us? Tell me something that you are liking about today's game. Like when I say like what you're seeing this season, what are you liking as a whole in this league? I I get it's not just us and you, it's sometimes we get tired of the, you know, these are the things that we don't like. So here's an opportunity for all of us to speak on something that we've enjoyed watching, not an individual, but a stylistic version of play that we've enjoyed watching at the start of the season.
quotes.social_post: Channing Frye on NBA defense: The teams that are going to be there at the end are the teams that defend. We all know that.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on his sacrifice during his 15th season
quotes.excerpt: I wanted to do whatever it took to be a part of the group.
quotes.quote: James Jones was big in keeping us there, but I was at year 15, so the sacrifice for me was different. I wanted to do whatever it took to be a part of the group. Those days were long behind me. I knew what my role was, so it was also part of my job as a person that wanted to win was to help convince people of their roles.
quotes.social_post: Richard Jefferson on his 15th season: The sacrifice for me was different. I wanted to do whatever it took to be a part of the group. It was part of my job to help convince people of their roles.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Grant Hill teaching Channing Frye to accept a specialized role
quotes.excerpt: Accept that role in that place for winning. It's going to suck, but just look at me.
quotes.quote: When I got to Phoenix, Grant Hill was like, listen, people are going to talk shit about you. People are going to say you're this or you're that, but we're going to win. He goes, Channing, Steve is a two-time MVP, Amar'e Stoudemire is like a four-time All-Star. You see Jason Richardson, he's like a two or three-time All-Star. He goes, you standing right here and doing your job and being available to shoot and working on that creates opportunities for everyone else to play four-on-four basketball. He goes, people are going to say why isn't he posting up? Are you a better post-up guy than Robin Lopez or Amar'e Stoudemire? I go, no. He goes, are you the best three-point shooter on our team? He goes, yeah. So accept that role in that place for winning. He goes, it's going to suck, but just look at me, I'm Grant Hill. I run the floor. The only points I get, or if I run the floor and do that cut, you know, you used to do that football face cut, right? The little inside post route. And he goes, or I stand in the corner. He goes, Channing, it's just who I am, and my opportunities don't come very often, but I believe in the All-Stars that we have, I believe in our leaders, and this is accepting a role and you star in that role.
quotes.social_post: Richard Jefferson on Grant Hill: Grant told me to accept my role as a shooter. He said it is going to suck, but it creates opportunities for everyone else to play four on four basketball.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson convincing Channing Frye to simplify his game in Cleveland
quotes.excerpt: We all got to eat less, but we're all going to eat at the buffet.
quotes.quote: When I got to Cleveland, I was like, Channing, we know you're great. I respect the shit out of Channing. Channing is very talented. But Channing compared to talent, compared to Kevin, Kyrie, J.R. Smith, and LeBron, you got to simplify your game so that your consistency we can rely on. And that was my attitude towards it. It's like, dude, look what Kevin is doing. Fucking Kevin, we had arguments, is Kevin the best power forward versus Tim Duncan? Like those are real arguments. And now Kevin is doing Channing Frye things to win. So brother, we all got to eat less, but we're all going to eat at the buffet at the end of it.
quotes.social_post: Richard Jefferson on the 2016 Cavs: I told Channing to simplify his game. We had Kevin Love doing Channing Frye things to win. We all had to eat less, but we were all going to eat at the buffet at the end of it.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins on the trade for Channing Frye and Richard Jefferson
quotes.excerpt: The trade that happened to get Channing and Swish wasn't for Swish. Chump was just injured.
quotes.quote: Let me say this, and I got to applaud y'all. I don't want to take up too much time, but I do got to get this off my chest. I got to give y'all flowers because Chump needed that. Y'all have to realize before y'all got there, I was there, and the trade that happened to get Chump and Swish wasn't for Swish. Chump was just injured, and then all of a sudden Swish stepped into a role because he was almost a throw-in into that trade and got an opportunity, and then he capitalized because he started to make shots. And then Bron wrapped his arm around him, and all of a sudden Bron taught Swish another level of professionalism. So Chump had to come in to a point of almost proving himself, right? Proving himself. So when it got to y'all year, the year that y'all won it, and I'm so fucking pissed off about that year because y'all did try to trade for me, and this fucking Dell Demps, who is one of the guys that I hate. No, I don't hate a lot of people, but I can't stand that motherfucker. He lied to me. He didn't trade me.
quotes.social_post: Kendrick Perkins: I am so pissed off about that year because y'all tried to trade for me and Dell Demps lied to me. I cannot stand that motherfucker.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kevin Garnett setting the tone for the 2008 Celtics
quotes.excerpt: Kevin Garnett set the tone from the jump, the first day of training camp in Rome.
quotes.quote: Kevin Garnett set the tone from the jump, the first day of training camp in Rome. He came in and he said, Doc, before you get started, we're going to run this offense through Paul and Ray. The world knew that Kevin Garnett was the best player on our team. He was the best player on our team, the only player with an MVP. No, we're going to run this offense. If you need me, I'm here, I'm going to focus defensively. That set the tone early.
quotes.social_post: Kendrick Perkins on Kevin Garnett: KG set the tone from the jump. He said we are going to run this offense through Paul and Ray. The world knew he was the best player, but he focused defensively.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: The difficulty of sacrificing individual goals for championship success
quotes.excerpt: It's one thing to talk about it and have the talent, but the hardest thing is the sacrifice.
quotes.quote: Outside of having the talent, the two most important things to winning a championship is health and sacrificing. If you're not going to sacrifice, you're not going to win. I went to the NBA Finals five times, I won once. And the one time that I won is because everybody lost themselves in the team. It's one thing to talk about it and have the talent, but the hardest thing in the world is the sacrifice.
quotes.social_post: Kendrick Perkins on winning: The two most important things to winning a championship is health and sacrificing. The one time I won is because everybody lost themselves in the team.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on Channing Frye's growth as a veteran leader
quotes.excerpt: I'm proud of Chump because he was very combative at the time, but as he became a veteran.
quotes.quote: I'm proud of Chump because he was very combative at the time, but as he became a veteran and got older, he understood, and now he's echoing that message to the next generation. And I think that's the greatest thing that we can do with this platform is teach the next generation the lessons we learned, the sacrifices we made.
quotes.social_post: Richard Jefferson: I am proud of Channing because he was combative, but he understood his role and now he is echoing that message to the next generation.
